title: Tashbar Math Ladder
status: PLAN ONLY, waiting for Mrs. Khaver. Nothing is built from it until she approves it.
asked: Mrs. Khaver (2026-11-24): "I don't want to work on faster or grade. I want to map the progression of skills and the most efficient way to teach each one."
how: Math is 11 ladders, side by side. Each rung is one real skill, in the order a child's thinking grows.
There are no grades on the ladder. Each rung says what must come first ("needs"), even from another ladder.
A short placement check finds his rung on each ladder. He moves up when he passes a rung's check with no help, two days apart.
If he gets stuck twice, he drops to the rung it needs for a short re-teach, then climbs back.
Every rung is taught the same way: an object he can move, then a picture, then the written rule. One clear idea in plain words. A worked example, then his turn. The usual mistake is shown and fixed.
Every practice set mixes in earlier rungs, so nothing is forgotten.
sources: Building Blocks (Clements & Sarama): the order of the early rungs and their level names.
Singapore: the bar model, and object, then picture, then rule.
Japan and China: few skills, taught deeply; meaning before shortcut rules.
Russia (Davydov, Toom): part–whole thinking and word problems before algebra.
Research on fractions (Siegler), mixed practice (Rohrer) and worked examples.
The report "The World's Best Math Programs for Grades 3–8" (November 2026).

strands.name: Counting and the number line
strands.about: Saying numbers, counting things, counting on and back, skip counting, then the whole number line: negatives, fractions and roots.

rungs.name: Say the numbers to 10
rungs.can: Says 1 to 10 in order, without skipping.
rungs.check: Count with me from 1. Where did you stop?

rungs.name: One number for each thing
rungs.can: Touches each thing once and says one number for it.
rungs.check: Count these 6 apples. Touch each one.

rungs.name: The last number tells how many
rungs.can: After counting, knows the last number is how many there are.
rungs.check: You counted 1 to 5. So how many are there?

rungs.name: Give me 7
rungs.can: Counts out a number of things when asked, to 10, then 20.
rungs.check: Put 7 kugels on the plate.
rungs.src: Building Blocks: Producer; Counter and Producer (10+)

rungs.name: One more, one less, count back
rungs.can: Counts back from 10. Knows the number just after and just before.
rungs.check: There are 6. One more comes. How many now, without counting all?
rungs.src: Building Blocks: Counter Backward; Counter from N (N+1, N–1)

rungs.name: Count to 100 by ones and tens
rungs.can: Counts to 100 by ones and by tens.
rungs.check: Count by tens to 100.
rungs.src: Building Blocks: Skip Counter by 10s; Counter to 100

rungs.name: Start anywhere and count on
rungs.can: Starts at any number (like 47) and counts on, to 120.
rungs.check: Start at 58. Count on 5.
rungs.src: Building Blocks: Counter On Using Patterns

rungs.name: Skip count; odd and even
rungs.can: Skip counts by 2s, 5s and 10s from any number. Tells odd from even by pairing.
rungs.check: Count by 5s from 35. Is 14 odd or even? Show me with pairs.

rungs.name: Count to 1,000 by 1s, 10s and 100s
rungs.can: Counts on and back by ones, tens and hundreds anywhere to 1,000.
rungs.check: Count by tens from 370 to 450.

rungs.name: Below zero: negative numbers
rungs.can: Places negatives on the number line, compares them, and uses all four parts of a grid.
rungs.check: Which is colder, –8° or –3°? Put both on the line.

rungs.name: All the numbers on one line
rungs.can: Puts fractions, decimals and negatives on one line. Knows which decimals end and which repeat.
rungs.check: Put –1½, 0.75 and –0.3 on the line.

rungs.name: Roots and real numbers
rungs.can: Finds square roots and squeezes a root between two whole numbers.
rungs.check: √50 is between which two whole numbers?

strands.name: Seeing, comparing and breaking numbers
strands.about: Seeing how many at a glance, comparing amounts, and knowing the parts inside a number. This is the ground that adding stands on.

rungs.name: See 1, 2, 3 at a glance
rungs.can: Says how many (up to 3, then 4) without counting.
rungs.check: Flash 3 dots for one second. How many?

rungs.name: See 5 at a glance
rungs.can: Sees up to 5 at once in dice and finger patterns.
rungs.check: Flash a 5 on a dice. How many?

rungs.name: More, fewer, the same
rungs.can: Compares two groups by matching or counting, even when one is spread out.
rungs.check: 7 spread-out cups and 8 close-together cups. Which has more?
rungs.src: Building Blocks: Matching Comparer; Counting Comparer

rungs.name: Parts of numbers to 5
rungs.can: Knows 5 is 4 and 1, 3 and 2.
rungs.check: 5 apples, 2 in the bag. How many are hiding?

rungs.name: Parts of 6 to 10; friends of 10
rungs.can: Knows all pairs that make 10, and the parts of 6 to 9.
rungs.check: 7 on the ten-frame. How many more make 10?

rungs.name: See numbers to 20 in parts
rungs.can: Sees "10 and 4" on ten-frames without counting.
rungs.check: Flash two ten-frames (10 and 6). How many?

rungs.name: Compare with < > =
rungs.can: Compares numbers by the biggest place first and writes < > =.
rungs.check: Which is more, 49 or 52? Write it with the sign.

strands.name: Adding and subtracting
strands.about: From joining things with his hands, to smart strategies, to written methods for big numbers, decimals and negatives.

rungs.name: Put together, take away (within 5)
rungs.can: Joins and takes away with things he can move.
rungs.check: Moshe has 3 cookies. Bubby gives him 2. How many now?
rungs.src: Building Blocks: Small Number +/–; Find Result

rungs.name: Add and take away within 10
rungs.can: Adds and subtracts within 10, including "how many more?".

rungs.name: Count on, count back
rungs.can: Adds by counting on from the bigger number, not from 1.
rungs.check: 8 + 3: start at 8 and hop.

rungs.name: Smart facts: doubles and make ten
rungs.can: Uses doubles, near doubles and make-ten within 20.
rungs.check: 8 + 6: make a ten first. Show me.

rungs.name: The = sign means "the same as"
rungs.can: Finds a missing number anywhere and judges true or false number sentences.

rungs.name: Facts within 20, fast
rungs.can: Knows every fact within 20 without counting.
rungs.check: 20 mixed facts in 2 minutes.

rungs.name: Add and subtract within 100
rungs.can: Adds and subtracts two-digit numbers by tens and ones, in his head and on a number line.

rungs.name: Written method within 1,000
rungs.can: Adds and subtracts with regrouping in columns.

rungs.name: Estimate first, then check
rungs.can: Rounds to estimate and tells if an answer makes sense.

rungs.name: Big numbers in columns
rungs.can: Adds and subtracts any whole numbers in columns.

rungs.name: Adding and subtracting decimals
rungs.can: Lines up the places to add and subtract decimals.

rungs.name: Adding and subtracting negatives
rungs.can: Adds and subtracts with negatives on a number line.

strands.name: Place value and big numbers
strands.about: Tens and ones, then hundreds, thousands and millions, then tenths and hundredths. Each place is 10 times the next.

rungs.name: Teen numbers: ten and some more
rungs.can: Sees 14 as one ten and 4 ones.
rungs.check: Show 16 with a ten-stick and cubes.
rungs.src: Building Blocks: Composer with Tens and Ones

rungs.name: Tens and ones to 100
rungs.can: Builds and reads any two-digit number as tens and ones.
rungs.check: How many tens in 73? Build it.
rungs.src: Building Blocks: Counter of Quantitative Units

rungs.name: 10 more, 10 less
rungs.can: Finds 10 more or 10 less in his head.
rungs.check: 10 less than 64?

rungs.name: Hundreds, tens and ones
rungs.can: Reads, writes, builds and compares numbers to 1,000, and in expanded form.
rungs.check: Write 406 as hundreds + tens + ones.

rungs.name: Round to estimate
rungs.can: Rounds to the nearest 10 and 100 on a number line.
rungs.check: Round 348 to the nearest ten and hundred.

rungs.name: Big numbers to a million
rungs.can: Knows each place is 10 times the next. Reads, compares and rounds big numbers.
rungs.check: How much bigger is the 7 in 7,000 than in 700?

rungs.name: Decimal places and powers of ten
rungs.can: Reads and compares decimals to thousandths. Multiplies and divides by 10, 100, 1,000.
rungs.check: Which is more, 0.4 or 0.38? 3.6 × 100?

rungs.name: Exponents and scientific notation
rungs.can: Uses powers and writes very big and very small numbers in scientific notation.
rungs.check: Write 45,000,000 in scientific notation.

strands.name: Multiplying and dividing
strands.about: From fair sharing, to equal groups and arrays, to facts known by heart, to written methods.

rungs.name: Fair sharing
rungs.can: Shares things fairly, one for you, one for me, and checks it is fair.
rungs.check: Share 8 pretzels fairly between 2 brothers.
rungs.src: Building Blocks: Beginning Grouper and Distributive Sharer

rungs.name: Equal groups; skip counting
rungs.can: Counts equal groups by skip counting.
rungs.check: 5 plates, 2 rolls on each. How many rolls?

rungs.name: Arrays and what × means
rungs.can: Knows 3 × 4 means 3 groups of 4. Sees rows and columns. Order does not matter.
rungs.check: Draw 3 × 4 two ways.

rungs.name: What ÷ means
rungs.can: Knows dividing as sharing and as making groups. Uses a times fact to divide.
rungs.check: 24 hamantaschen, 6 on each plate. How many plates?

rungs.name: Times facts with strategies
rungs.can: Finds hard facts from easy ones (double the 2s to get the 4s).
rungs.check: You know 5 × 7. How does it help with 6 × 7?

rungs.name: Times facts by heart
rungs.can: Knows every fact to 10 × 10 instantly. This is a gate: long division waits for it.
rungs.check: 40 mixed facts in 3 minutes.
rungs.src: Japan, China, Saxon; research on fluency

rungs.name: Times tens and hundreds
rungs.can: Multiplies by 10s and 100s using place value (4 × 60).

rungs.name: Multi-digit multiplying
rungs.can: Multiplies with an area model, then the standard written method.

rungs.name: Long division (1-digit divisor)
rungs.can: Divides in writing and decides what a leftover means.
rungs.check: 50 boys, 6 to a van. How many vans?

rungs.name: Factors, multiples, primes
rungs.can: Finds all factor pairs to 100. Tells prime from composite.
rungs.check: All the factors of 36. Is 29 prime?

rungs.name: Two-digit divisors; × ÷ decimals
rungs.can: Divides by 2-digit numbers. Multiplies and divides decimals.

rungs.name: Common factors and multiples
rungs.can: Finds the greatest common factor and least common multiple.
rungs.check: GCF of 24 and 36.

rungs.name: × ÷ with negatives
rungs.can: Multiplies and divides with negative numbers and fractions.

strands.name: Fractions, decimals, ratio and percent
strands.about: The gateway to algebra. From fair halves of a challah, to fractions as numbers on a line, to all four operations, to percent and ratio.

rungs.name: Fair shares
rungs.can: Cuts a whole into equal parts and knows equal means the same size, not the same shape.
rungs.check: Is this challah cut in fair halves? Why not?

teach.see: Paper folding, then a picture of a challah, pizza or chocolate bar cut into parts.
teach.say: "Fair" means every piece is the same size. Count the pieces to name them: 2 fair pieces are halves, 4 fair pieces are fourths.
steps: Fold a paper in half. Do the two parts match exactly?
Cut a picture into 2, 3, then 4 fair pieces.
Say fair or not fair, and tell why.
teach.mistake: He calls any 2 pieces "halves", even when one is bigger. Fix: lay one piece on the other. If they do not match, it is not fair.
teach.practice: Fair or not fair: tap to judge. Cut it fairly: drag a knife line. Two different-looking halves of a square: are both fair?
teach.why: Children understand fair sharing long before they understand fraction symbols. Starting here builds on what they already know.

rungs.name: One part: unit fractions
rungs.can: Names one part of equal parts as 1/2, 1/3, 1/4. Knows more parts means smaller pieces.
rungs.check: Which piece is bigger, 1/8 or 1/4 of the same cake?

teach.see: Fraction strips: the same long strip cut into 2, 3, 4, 6 and 8 equal parts, laid one above the other.
teach.say: The bottom number tells how many equal parts the whole has. The more parts, the smaller each one.
steps: Take one strip. Count its equal parts. That tells the bottom number.
One part is "one ___th".
Lay strips under each other to compare.
teach.mistake: He thinks 1/8 is bigger than 1/4 "because 8 is bigger than 4". Fix: show both pieces side by side on strips, and share one cake among 8 brothers vs 4 brothers.
teach.practice: Name the piece. Order 1/2, 1/8, 1/3, 1/6 from biggest to smallest. "Would you rather have 1/3 or 1/5 of the kugel?"
teach.why: Unit fractions are the building block of all other fractions; Japan and Singapore start every fraction topic from them.

rungs.name: Fractions are counted in units
rungs.can: Sees 3/4 as three 1/4s, and counts on by unit fractions past 1.
rungs.check: How many fourths make 3/4? What comes after 4/4?

teach.see: Fraction strips, then tiles of one unit fraction counted out one by one.
teach.say: We count fourths the way we count apples: one fourth, two fourths, three fourths, four fourths, five fourths.
steps: Pick the unit (one fourth).
Count how many units.
Say it: "three fourths" = 3/4.
teach.mistake: He reads 3/4 as "3 and 4", two separate numbers. Fix: always say it as a count of units ("three fourths") and build it from unit tiles.
teach.practice: Build 5/6 from sixths. Count on: 2/3, 3/3, 4/3, __. Which is made of more pieces?
teach.why: Seeing a fraction as a count of unit fractions makes adding fractions and fractions bigger than 1 obvious later.

rungs.name: Fractions on the number line
rungs.can: Places fractions between 0 and 1 and beyond 1. Knows a fraction is a number, and 4/4 = 1.
rungs.check: Put 3/4 on the line. Where is 5/4?
rungs.src: Siegler: fraction size on the number line predicts later algebra

teach.see: A measuring tape or a long strip, then a number line from 0 to 1 cut into equal spaces.
teach.say: The whole is the distance from 0 to 1. Cut it into equal spaces. Each space is one unit fraction long.
steps: Find 0 and 1.
Cut the space between them into equal parts (the bottom number).
Count the spaces from 0 (the top number).
teach.mistake: He counts tick marks instead of spaces, so 3/4 lands in the wrong place. Fix: hop along the spaces from 0, saying "one fourth, two fourths…".
teach.practice: Drag the fraction to its place. Find 1 on a line where only 0 and 1/3 are marked. Spot the wrong label.
teach.why: Placing fractions on a line is the strongest early sign of later algebra success, so this rung is the heart of the ladder.

rungs.name: Compare fractions
rungs.can: Compares using the same bottom, the same top, or a benchmark of 1/2 and 1.
rungs.check: Which is more, 3/8 or 3/5? 5/8 or 4/10? Explain.

teach.see: Two number lines or two strips, one above the other.
teach.say: Same-size pieces: more pieces is more. Same number of pieces: bigger pieces is more. Or check: is it more or less than a half?
steps: Same bottom? Compare the tops.
Same top? The smaller bottom means bigger pieces.
Neither? Compare each to 1/2 or to 1.
teach.mistake: He compares only the top numbers or only the bottom numbers. Fix: always ask "how big is each piece?" and check on the line.
teach.practice: Tap the bigger fraction. Put 3 fractions in order. "Explain why" taps a reason, not just an answer.
teach.why: Reasoning about size, not following a rule, is what makes fraction work stick.

rungs.name: Equal fractions
rungs.can: Finds equal fractions by splitting every piece. Then the rule: multiply top and bottom by the same number.

teach.see: A strip folded in half, then folded again: the half is now 2 fourths, then 4 eighths.
teach.say: Cutting every piece into 2 makes twice as many pieces, each half as big. The amount stays the same.
steps: Draw the fraction.
Split every piece into the same number of smaller pieces.
Count the new pieces: top and bottom were both multiplied.
teach.mistake: He adds the same number to top and bottom (1/2 = 2/3). Fix: draw both. They do not cover the same amount.
teach.practice: Match equal fractions. Fill the missing number. Simplify 6/8 by grouping pieces back together.
teach.why: Equal fractions are the tool for comparing, adding unlike fractions and later ratio. The picture keeps the rule from feeling like magic.

rungs.name: Add and subtract like fractions; mixed numbers
rungs.can: Adds and subtracts fractions with the same bottom, including mixed numbers.

teach.see: Hops on a number line, and unit tiles.
teach.say: 2 fifths plus 4 fifths is 6 fifths, the same way 2 apples plus 4 apples is 6 apples. The bottom names the piece. It does not change.
steps: Check the pieces are the same size (same bottom).
Add or take away the number of pieces.
Change extra wholes: 6/5 = 1 1/5.
teach.mistake: He adds the bottoms too (2/5 + 4/5 = 6/10). Fix: say it in words ("fifths plus fifths are fifths") and check it is bigger than each part.
teach.practice: Add with tiles, then without. Regroup a mixed number like trading a ten. Find the mistake in a worked example.
teach.why: Counting units makes the right answer obvious and blocks the most common fraction error.

rungs.name: Tenths and hundredths as decimals
rungs.can: Writes tenths and hundredths as decimals and compares them.
rungs.check: 0.7 = ?/100. Which is more, 0.25 or 0.3?

teach.see: Money (dimes and pennies), a meter stick, a 10 × 10 grid.
teach.say: The places keep going to the right of the ones: tenths, then hundredths. Each place is 10 times smaller.
steps: Read the fraction with a bottom of 10 or 100.
Write it in places after the point.
Compare place by place, starting from the left.
teach.mistake: He thinks 0.25 is bigger than 0.3 because "25 is bigger than 3". Fix: shade both on a hundred grid, or say them as money: 25¢ vs 30¢.
teach.practice: Shade the grid. Write it as a decimal. Put decimals in order on a line.
teach.why: Decimals are fractions written in place value. Linking the two avoids treating decimals as whole numbers with a dot.

rungs.name: Add and subtract unlike fractions
rungs.can: Finds a common piece size, then adds or subtracts.

teach.see: Two strips with different cuts, both cut further until the pieces match.
teach.say: You can only add pieces that are the same size. Cut both into the same size pieces first.
steps: Find a bottom number both can become (a common multiple).
Change each fraction into an equal fraction.
Add or subtract the pieces.
teach.mistake: He adds across: 2/3 + 1/4 = 3/7. Fix: estimate first. 2/3 + 1/4 is more than 2/3, and 3/7 is less than 1/2, so it is wrong.
teach.practice: Split the strips to match. Solve, then check with an estimate. Spot the wrong method.
teach.why: Builds directly on equal fractions (FR6), so it is a short step, not a new rule to memorize.

rungs.name: A fraction of an amount
rungs.can: Finds 3/4 of 20 with a bar model, and multiplies a fraction by a whole number.

teach.see: A bar model: one bar for the whole amount, cut into equal parts.
teach.say: Cut the whole into 4 equal parts. One part is 20 ÷ 4 = 5. Three parts are 15.
steps: Draw a bar for the whole and write its amount.
Cut it into equal parts (the bottom number) and find one part.
Take the number of parts (the top number).
teach.mistake: He multiplies 20 × 4 or divides by the top number. Fix: draw the bar every time until it is automatic.
teach.practice: 3/5 of the 30 boys go on the trip. How many? Story problems with bars that fill in, then bars he draws.
teach.why: The bar model turns "fraction of" into simple division and multiplication, and it is the same picture used later for ratio and percent.

rungs.name: Fraction times fraction
rungs.can: Multiplies fractions with an area model, then the rule. Knows multiplying by less than 1 makes it smaller.
rungs.check: 2/3 × 3/4. Is 5 × 2/3 more or less than 5?

teach.see: Fold a paper into thirds one way and fourths the other way. Shade 2/3 of 3/4.
teach.say: 2/3 × 3/4 means "2/3 of 3/4". Multiply the tops to count shaded pieces, and the bottoms to count all the pieces.
steps: Shade the first fraction.
Take a fraction of the shaded part.
Count: top × top over bottom × bottom.
teach.mistake: He thinks multiplying always makes bigger. Fix: "half of 6 is 3". Taking a part of something makes it smaller.
teach.practice: Shade and solve. Bigger or smaller than the starting number? Recipe problems: 2/3 of a 3/4-cup measure.
teach.why: The area picture explains the rule, so he can rebuild it if he forgets.

rungs.name: Dividing with fractions
rungs.can: Answers "how many 1/4s in 3?" with strips. Then common bottoms. Then why "flip and multiply" works.
rungs.src: Japan, Singapore, Russia: meaning before rule

teach.see: Strips: lay 1/4 pieces along 3 wholes and count them.
teach.say: Dividing asks "how many of these fit in that?". 3 ÷ 1/4 asks how many quarters fit in 3. 12.
steps: Ask the "how many fit" question.
With the same bottom, divide the tops.
Shortcut: multiply by the flipped divisor (show why with one example).
teach.mistake: He flips the wrong fraction, or flips both. Fix: estimate with the "how many fit" question first.
teach.practice: How many 1/3-cup scoops in 2 cups? Strips, then common bottoms, then the shortcut. Find the wrong flip.
teach.why: Japan and Singapore teach this rung only after the meaning is clear. That keeps it from being the most-forgotten rule in school math.

rungs.name: Percent
rungs.can: Knows percent means "out of 100". Finds 10%, 25%, 50% and any percent of an amount.
rungs.check: 20% of 45. What percent is 18 out of 24?
rungs.src: Singapore bar model; Dutch double number line

teach.see: A 10 × 10 grid, then a bar marked 0% to 100%, then a double number line.
teach.say: Percent means "out of 100". The whole bar is 100%. 10% is one tenth of it.
steps: Draw a bar for 100%.
Find 10% (divide by 10) or 1%.
Build the percent you need from those.
teach.mistake: He thinks 20% of 45 is 20, or adds the percent. Fix: start from the 100% bar and find 10% first.
teach.practice: Shade percents. Discount and tip stories with bars. Benchmarks: is 48% about a half?
teach.why: Builds on fractions and decimals with the same bar picture, so percent is not a separate topic to learn.

rungs.name: Ratio and rate
rungs.can: Uses ratio tables and bar models. Finds a unit rate.
rungs.check: 3 bottles cost $6. What do 7 cost? Boys to girls 2:3.

teach.see: A ratio table and a bar model with equal units.
teach.say: A ratio compares two amounts in the same units. Find the price of one, then any number.
steps: Write both amounts in a table.
Find the amount for 1 (unit rate).
Multiply to get the amount you need.
teach.mistake: He adds the same amount to both sides (2:3 becomes 4:5) instead of multiplying. Fix: check with the table that both sides were multiplied.
teach.practice: Recipe scaling for a simcha. Better buy: which pack is cheaper per item? Fill in ratio tables.
teach.why: Ratio is the bridge from arithmetic to algebra. It uses multiplying, not adding.

rungs.name: Proportions and percent change
rungs.can: Spots proportional relationships, writes y = kx, and solves discount, tax and percent-change problems.
rungs.check: A $40 coat is 15% off. What does it cost?

teach.see: A before-and-after bar model and a straight-line graph through 0.
teach.say: When two amounts grow together at the same rate, one is always k times the other.
steps: Check that the rate stays the same.
Find k (the amount for 1).
Use y = kx or a before-and-after bar.
teach.mistake: He takes 15% off and then adds tax to the wrong amount. Fix: draw the before-and-after bar for each step.
teach.practice: Is it proportional? Find k from a table or graph. Discount and interest stories.
teach.why: Finishes the fraction ladder and leads straight into linear functions (PA10).

strands.name: Story problems with bar models
strands.about: One picture, the bar model, used from first stories to algebra. Every story problem is drawn first, then solved.

rungs.name: Act it out
rungs.can: Acts out joining and taking-away stories with things.
rungs.check: Act out: 3 boys, then 2 more come.

rungs.name: Part–part–whole bar
rungs.can: Draws a bar with two parts and a whole, and finds the missing piece.
rungs.check: 9 seforim: 4 on the table, the rest on the shelf. How many on the shelf?

rungs.name: Compare bar
rungs.can: Draws two bars to show "how many more" or "how many fewer".
rungs.check: Chaim has 13 marbles, 5 more than Dovid. How many has Dovid?

rungs.name: Two-step stories
rungs.can: Draws bars for stories with two steps and an unknown anywhere.
rungs.check: A story that needs + then –.

rungs.name: Equal-groups bar
rungs.can: Draws equal units for multiplying and dividing stories.
rungs.check: 6 boxes of 8 candies. How many?

rungs.name: "Times as many" bar
rungs.can: Draws one bar 3 times as long as another.
rungs.check: Yossi has 4 times as many stickers as Shmuel. Together 40. How many each?

rungs.name: Fraction-of bar
rungs.can: Draws stories with a fraction of an amount.
rungs.check: 3/5 of the class went. 12 stayed. How many in the class?

rungs.name: Ratio bar
rungs.can: Draws stories with ratios in equal units.
rungs.check: Apples to pears is 2:3. 30 fruits. How many apples?

rungs.name: Before-and-after percent bar
rungs.can: Draws percent increase and decrease stories.
rungs.check: The price went up 20% to $60. What was it before?

rungs.name: From bar to equation
rungs.can: Writes the bar as an equation with a letter for the unknown bar.
rungs.check: Draw the bar, then write 4x + x = 40.

strands.name: Patterns and algebra
strands.about: From AB patterns on a bead string, to number rules, to letters, equations and graphs.

rungs.name: Copy and continue AB patterns
rungs.can: Copies and continues red-blue-red-blue.
rungs.check: What comes next? Finish the bead string.
rungs.src: Building Blocks: Pattern Duplicator AB; Extender AB

rungs.name: The part that repeats
rungs.can: Finds the core of ABB and ABC patterns, fixes a broken one, makes his own.
rungs.check: Circle the part that repeats.

rungs.name: Number patterns
rungs.can: Continues and explains patterns like 5, 10, 15 or +10 on a hundred chart.
rungs.check: 14, 24, 34, __. What is the rule?

rungs.name: Patterns with a rule
rungs.can: Finds and explains the rule in a number pattern or times table.
rungs.check: Why does every multiple of 5 end in 0 or 5?

rungs.name: Order of operations; expressions
rungs.can: Writes and works out expressions with brackets, in the right order.

rungs.name: Letters for numbers
rungs.can: Uses a letter for an unknown or a changing amount.
rungs.check: What is 3n when n = 4? Write "5 more than x".

rungs.name: One-step equations and inequalities
rungs.can: Solves x + 9 = 23 and 3x = 21, and shows x > 4 on a line.

rungs.name: Two-step equations
rungs.can: Solves two-step equations and simplifies expressions, with negatives and fractions.

rungs.name: Graph a relationship
rungs.can: Makes a table, plots it, and sees whether the points make a straight line.
rungs.check: Plot the cost of 1 to 5 bottles at $2 each.

rungs.name: Linear functions and slope
rungs.can: Knows what a function is. Finds slope. Graphs and writes y = mx + b.
rungs.check: Graph y = 2x + 1. What is the slope?

rungs.name: Two equations at once
rungs.can: Solves a system of two linear equations by graph and by reasoning.
rungs.check: x + y = 10 and x – y = 2.

strands.name: Shapes and space
strands.about: From naming shapes by their rules, to building with shapes, to angles, area, volume and short proofs.

rungs.name: Name shapes by their rules
rungs.can: Names circle, triangle, square and rectangle in any size or turn.
rungs.check: Find all the triangles, even the upside-down one.

rungs.name: Sides and corners; tricky look-alikes
rungs.can: Counts sides and corners. Knows a shape with a gap or curve is not a triangle.
rungs.check: Is this a triangle? Why not?

rungs.name: Solid shapes
rungs.can: Names sphere, cube, cylinder and cone; knows flat from solid.
rungs.check: Which one rolls? Which stacks?

rungs.name: Where is it?
rungs.can: Uses on top, under, next to, in front of, behind.
rungs.check: Put the cup behind the box.

rungs.name: Build shapes from shapes
rungs.can: Puts shapes together to make new shapes and pictures, and plans which piece goes where.
rungs.check: Make a hexagon with triangles.
rungs.src: Building Blocks: Picture Maker; Shape Composer

rungs.name: Turn and flip in your mind
rungs.can: Pictures a shape turned or flipped and finds the match.
rungs.check: Which piece fits the gap?

rungs.name: Rows and columns
rungs.can: Cuts a rectangle into rows and columns of same-size squares and counts them.
rungs.check: Fill this rectangle with squares. How many?

rungs.name: Four-sided shape families
rungs.can: Sorts quadrilaterals by their properties. Knows a square is also a rectangle.
rungs.check: Is a square a rectangle? Prove it.

rungs.name: The coordinate grid
rungs.can: Plots and reads points on a grid.
rungs.check: Plot (3, 5).

rungs.name: Angles, lines and symmetry
rungs.can: Measures and draws angles. Finds parallel lines and lines of symmetry.
rungs.check: Measure this angle. Draw a line of symmetry.

rungs.name: Shape family tree
rungs.can: Places shapes in a family tree by their properties.
rungs.check: Every rhombus is a ___?
rungs.src: Building Blocks: Property Class Identifier; van Hiele

rungs.name: Area of triangles and parallelograms
rungs.can: Finds their area by cutting and rearranging into rectangles.
rungs.check: Area of a triangle with base 8 and height 5.
rungs.src: Japan: area by cutting and moving

rungs.name: Nets and surface area
rungs.can: Unfolds solids into nets and finds surface area.
rungs.check: Draw the net of a box. Find its surface area.

rungs.name: Circles
rungs.can: Finds circumference and area of a circle.
rungs.check: Area of a circle with radius 3.

rungs.name: Angle facts and scale drawings
rungs.can: Uses angle facts (straight line, triangle) and scale drawings.
rungs.check: Two angles of a triangle are 50° and 60°. The third?

rungs.name: Slide, turn, flip; short proofs
rungs.can: Describes moves on a grid and gives short reasons why two shapes are the same.
rungs.check: Show that these two triangles are the same size and shape.
rungs.src: Japan, China: short proofs; van Hiele

rungs.name: Pythagoras
rungs.can: Uses a² + b² = c².
rungs.check: A 13 ft ladder, foot 5 ft from the wall. How high?

rungs.name: Volume of round solids
rungs.can: Finds the volume of cylinders, cones and spheres.
rungs.check: Volume of a can with radius 3 and height 10.

strands.name: Measuring, time and money
strands.about: From lining things up to compare, to units with no gaps, to rulers, area, volume and changing units.

rungs.name: Longer, shorter, taller
rungs.can: Compares lengths by lining things up from the same start.
rungs.check: Which pencil is longer? Line them up first.

rungs.name: Heavier, lighter, holds more
rungs.can: Compares weight on a balance and how much cups hold.
rungs.check: Which is heavier? Look at the balance.

rungs.name: Measure with units, no gaps
rungs.can: Measures with same-size units laid end to end, with no gaps or overlaps.
rungs.check: How many paper clips long is the pencil?
rungs.src: Building Blocks: End-to-End Measurer; Unit Iterater

rungs.name: Use a ruler
rungs.can: Measures with a ruler starting at 0, in inches and centimeters.
rungs.check: Measure the line. How much longer is the blue one?

rungs.name: Time to the hour and half hour
rungs.can: Reads clocks to the hour and half hour.
rungs.check: What time is it?

rungs.name: Time to the minute; how long
rungs.can: Reads time to the minute and finds how long something took.
rungs.check: Davening starts 8:15, ends 8:50. How long?

rungs.name: Money
rungs.can: Names coins, counts money and makes change.
rungs.check: You pay $1 for a 65¢ snack. What change?

rungs.name: Area
rungs.can: Finds area by covering with squares, then by multiplying sides.
rungs.check: Area of a 6 × 4 room.

rungs.name: Perimeter
rungs.can: Finds the distance around, and tells it apart from area.
rungs.check: Same area, different perimeter: draw two.

rungs.name: Liquid and weight units
rungs.can: Measures in liters, milliliters, grams and kilograms (and cups, pounds).
rungs.check: Which holds about 1 liter: a cup or a bottle?

rungs.name: Change units
rungs.can: Changes feet to inches, hours to minutes, and metric units.
rungs.check: 3 ft 4 in = ? in. 2.5 kg = ? g.

rungs.name: Volume
rungs.can: Finds volume by packing cubes, then by length × width × height.
rungs.check: Volume of a 4 × 3 × 2 box.

rungs.name: Change units with ratios
rungs.can: Uses ratio reasoning to change any units.
rungs.check: 60 miles in 1 hour. How far in 20 minutes?

strands.name: Data and chance
strands.about: From sorting toys into bins, to graphs, to average and spread, to chance.

rungs.name: Sort and count
rungs.can: Sorts by color, size or shape, counts each group, says which has more.
rungs.check: Sort the toys. Which bin has the most?

rungs.name: Picture graphs
rungs.can: Reads and makes a picture graph and answers "how many more?".
rungs.check: How many more boys picked apples than pears?

rungs.name: Bar graphs
rungs.can: Makes and reads bar graphs.
rungs.check: Make a bar graph of 4 groups.

rungs.name: Graphs with a scale
rungs.can: Reads graphs where one picture or square stands for 2, 5 or 10.
rungs.check: Each star stands for 5. How many?

rungs.name: Line plots with fractions
rungs.can: Makes line plots of measurements in halves, fourths and eighths.
rungs.check: Plot these lengths: 2¼, 2½, 2¼, 3.

rungs.name: Average as a fair share
rungs.can: Finds the mean by evening out, then by adding and dividing.
rungs.check: Scores 6, 8, 10: even them out.

rungs.name: Middle and spread
rungs.can: Finds median and range. Reads dot plots and box plots.
rungs.check: 6, 8, 8, 9, 14: median and range?

rungs.name: Count the possibilities
rungs.can: Lists all the ways something can happen with a list, table or tree.
rungs.check: How many outfits from 3 shirts and 2 pants?

rungs.name: Chance
rungs.can: Finds the probability of simple events as a fraction.
rungs.check: 3 red and 5 blue in a bag. Chance of red?

rungs.name: Samples
rungs.can: Uses a fair sample to make a guess about a whole group.
rungs.check: 20 of 50 boys asked like soccer. About how many of 400?

rungs.name: Scatter plots and two-way tables
rungs.can: Draws a trend line and reads two-way tables.
rungs.check: Does more practice mean higher scores? Draw the line.

next: Mrs. Khaver checks the order of the rungs and what each one needs.
She checks the sample teaching plan on the Fractions ladder (FR1–FR15): is this the right kind of detail?
When she is happy with the sample, the same teaching plan is written for every other rung.
Only after the whole plan is approved does any building start, one rung at a time.
